The applicants namely, Anoop Kumar Chaurasia and Jitendra Kumar Chaurasia, by means of this application under Section 482 Cr.P.C., have invoked the inherent jurisdiction of the Court with prayer for setting aside charge-sheet No. 124 if 2011, dated 9.9.2011 as well as proceeding of Criminal CAse No. 400 of 2012,( State vs. Anoop Kumar Chaurasia and another), arising out of 259 of 2011, under Sections 272, 273 I.P.C., P.S. Atarra, District Banda, pending before the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Banda.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicants and learned A.G.A. for the State.

Learned counsel for the applicant argued that it was First Information Report got lodged as Case Crime No. 259 of 2011, P.S. Atarra, District Banda, under Sections272, 273 I.P.C., on 17.8.2011, at 19:30 P.M., upon the report of Chief Food Inspector, Vijay Prashad Singh, against applicants, for an Anoop Kumar Chaurasia And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 23 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193549881/
1 alleged occurrence of 10.2.2011 at 3:15 P.M., with this contention that Chief Food Inspecotr, Banda,
was at his duty at town of Atarra, when Satya Narayan Pandey- Food Inspector and Rakesh Kumar Srivastava along with Devi Prasad Sharma, both of Food Inspectors met them.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: They went at the shop of Anoop Kumar Chaurasia, situated at Gandhi Chauk, Atarra.
They introduced themselves and asked that food articles being sold by above shop, is having report of adulteration and contamination.
The licence for the year 2010-11 was asked to be shown but shop keeper failed for it.
He apprised that Jitendra Kumar Chaurasiya, is the owner of shop and that can be shown by him.

But from that shop Dilruba Shahi Gutkha (packed) and Tulsa Pan Samagri (packed), was purchased for a consideration and following Rules given under Rules of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,
same was packed, sealed with preparation of specimen seal and it was sent for analysis at food laboratory where, it was found to be sub-standard because insoluble exceeded to prescribed limit of 0.5% from Pan Masala.
There was presence of Gambier as well as presence of Tobacco was there and this tobacco is injuries to health.
In addition of tobacco in any food article is prohibited under Rule 37-A-2(C) and Rule 44 (J) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and Rules made therein, 1955.

As specimen was adulterated and below standard, hence, H.R. Sharma, the then D.I.G.
Police/Additional Commissioner (Enforcement),
at the office of Food Commissioner at Lucknow,
vide its letter H/D/A/2001/3050, dated 29.7.2011, directed informant for getting case registered at police station concerned.
Hence, this report was got lodged.
Side by Side complaints were also filed for the same offence.
But in a proceeding before this Court, summoning in above complaint was dismissed.
Whereas, in this Criminal case charge-sheet was filed, over which cognizance was taken.
Hence, for ensuring end of justice, this application has been filed with above prayer.

Learned AGA has vehemently opposed the above prayer with this contention that First Information Report was got lodged for offences punishable under Sections 272 and 273 I.P.C. and it was investigated, thereafter, charge-sheet was filed, wherein, cognizance was taken.
The offence of adulteration under Special Act of Prevention of Food and Adulteration Act, is something else, for which F.S.S. Act will apply for I.P.C. cases there is no bar.

entities.text: Special Act of Prevention of Food and Adulteration Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Admittedly, the informant lodged this report, in compliance of direction given by Deputy Commissioner of Food and articles sent for analysis at laboratory, were found to be adulterated i.e.
there was infringement of standard, fixed for food material under Rules of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
This Act was replaced by Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006,

wherein,
notification was of 29th July, 2010.
Then after, all the provision of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act were merged with new act of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006.

This court in Writ Petition No 8254 (MB) of 2010, M/S Pepsi Co India Holdings vs State Of U.P. , by division Bench, has held that a prosecution under Section 272 and 273 of I.P.C., in the matter relating to adulteration of food articles is holly unjustified and applicants can only be proceeded in accordance with law and provision of Food Standard and Safety Act 2006.

entities.text: M/S Pepsi Co India Holdings vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of directions given by above Court, under same situation and facts as well as law discussed as above, the application merits to be allowed.
According, this application is being allowed.
